slides.title: Racing every three weeks but not getting faster?
slides.sub: Give every race gap a shape instead of improvising it

slides.title: Three weeks between races, one hard week
slides.caption: A default three week gap between races, with only the middle week hard.

slides.title: Week one: slow down, pay attention
slides.body: Keep skating but drop the intensity. Edges, deep position and slow crossovers. Speed hides faults, and this week you do not need speed.

slides.title: Week two: the only week you push
slides.body: Starts, race pace repetitions with full rest, and one technical fault for the whole week. Your heaviest off ice work sits here too.

slides.title: Week three: short and sharp
slides.body: Two ice sessions is plenty. Starts at full effort, a few race speed efforts, then stop. Sharpen three to five days before the first heat.

slides.title: Label your meets before the season
slides.body: Two or three are targets. The rest are training races where you try one experiment, like a new setup or a distance you avoid.

slides.text: Never cut the rest day to make room.
